column1: # The Computer Science Ontology as a term taxonomy: the topics computer science research is
# indexed by, each with the label CSO states for it and the equivalent labels it states beside it.
# CSO states NO definition for any topic, so this is matched against declared names like OLiA and
# FIBO and cannot be read as a functional taxonomy — there is no prose to compare a scope against.
# Columns: concept, prefLabel, altLabel, broader, kind, module, definition, note.
# definition is empty for every row because CSO publishes none.
# LOSSY, AND THE LOSS IS STATED. CSO is a poly-hierarchy: 9927 of its 14624 topics with a parent have
# more than one, up to 33, and the eight-column shape holds one broader. The alphabetically first
# is carried so a run reproduces, and 29886 parent statements are dropped. Branch corroboration read
# from this file is therefore reading a tree CSO did not publish. The shape has to change before
# any reading depends on the hierarchy.
# Source: CSO 3.5, https://cso.kmi.open.ac.uk/download (CSO.3.5.csv, sha of the archive recorded
#   by whoever fetched it — the download states no revision).
# Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) — "you can freely copy,
#   share, adapt, and build upon the data for any purpose, including commercial use, as long as
#   you give appropriate credit to the original creators". Redistribution in a published artefact
#   is therefore permitted with attribution, and NOTICE.md is where that credit is carried.
#   The downloaded archive itself states no licence and carries no licence file; these terms were
#   supplied by the maintainer of this repository rather than read from the archive, so the source
#   of the verdict is recorded here rather than implied.
# NOT BUNDLED YET, and not for licence reasons: no vocabulary is bundled until the extractors are
#   one runner, and the single-broader loss above has to be settled first.
